terms.meaning: Two expressions with an equal sign between them. The two sides are the LHS and the RHS.
The value of the letter-number that makes LHS = RHS.
The name for algebra in ancient India.

items.name: Keeping the balance
items.formula: Do the same thing to both sides
items.example: x + 5 = 12. Subtract 5 from both sides: x = 7.

items.name: Checking an answer
items.formula: Put it back and see if LHS = RHS

items.name: Moving a term across
items.formula: An added term moves across as a subtraction

items.name: Removing a multiplier
items.formula: Divide the other side by it

items.name: Removing a divisor
items.formula: Multiply the other side by it

items.name: Unknown on both sides
items.formula: Bring the unknowns to one side first

items.name: Equations with no solution
items.example: x + 4 = x + 5 has no solution, because 4 more can never equal 5 more.

items.name: A brick puzzle
items.formula: Let the unknown be a letter
items.example: A brick weighs 1 kg more than half its weight: b = 1 + b/2, so b = 2 kg.

items.name: Equal numbers of notes
items.formula: Count each kind by the same letter
items.example: n notes of ₹50 and n of ₹100 total ₹600: 150n = 600, so n = 4.

items.name: Heads and legs
items.formula: Let one kind be x, and the other the rest
items.example: 12 heads, 34 legs: 2x + 4(12 − x) = 34, so x = 7 hens and 5 cows.

mistakes.text: Change the sign when moving a term. 4x + 6 = 10 gives 4x = 10 − 6, not 10 + 6.
Divide the whole side, not one term. For 3x + 1 = 12, subtract 1 first: 3x = 11.
Do the same thing to both sides. Changing one side breaks the balance.
